goal.title: Explicit labels on every tool
criteria: The tool list an assistant receives shows the read-only, destructive and open-world labels on every tool, each with an explicit true or false, on the desktop and on the hosted playmat.
The reads are marked read-only, only starting a new game, importing a game and rebuilding it with an opponent list are marked destructive, and no tool is marked as reaching outside the playmat.
In the hosted playmat every tool declares that it needs the player's sign-in; on the desktop none does.
Tool names, arguments and results are unchanged, so Claude connects and plays as before.

(server.go:213, guides.go:30); a grep finds no other mcp.AddTool in internal/mcpserver. annotations_test.go TestToolLabelsExplicitOnTheWire checks the raw wire JSON for both servers over both transports. annotations.go:15-28 readOnlyTools lists ping, get_record, get_state, get_log, get_warnings, card_text, wait_for_turn, search_deck, look_top, list_branches, get_profile, guide. annotations.go:33-37 replacingTools is exactly new_game, import_log, set_opponent_deck. annotations.go:125 sets openWorldHint false on every tool, and annotations.go:43-48 does the same in the Go struct. items.title: Instructions that stand alone and waits inside the limit

goal.title: Instructions that stand alone and waits inside the limit
criteria: The first 512 characters of the playmat's instructions name what the playmat is, the rule to reference cards by their instance IDs, and where to find the coaching guides, as complete sentences.
The turn loop, the guide list and the hosted board-link line are still in the instructions.
A wait for a turn that is not over returns in under 60 seconds with a result telling the assistant to call it again.
The playmat refuses to start with a wait limit that could exceed ChatGPT's one-minute limit.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/mcpserver/server.go:88 defines openingInstructions as the first paragraph of instructions (line 73 prepends it). Its first three sentences name the playmat ("TCG Replay is a virtual Pokémon TCG playmat..."), the iid rule ("Refer to every card by its instance ID (iid, such as \"p2-12\"), never by name; get_state lists the iids.") and the guides ("Coaching workflows have guides: read the matching guide with the guide tool before you start one, or call guide with no name to list them."). Each is a complete sentence ending with a full stop. Counting characters, the paragraph ends at about 482 characters (about 483 bytes, since 'é' is two bytes), inside the 512-character window. TestInstructionsOpening in internal/mcpserver/guides_test.go:446 checks the same thing.

The turn loop is still in the instructions at server.go:83 ("After handing the player a turn ... call wait_for_turn ... calling it again until the turn ends"). The guide list is appended by s.instructions() at server.go:96 via guideInstructions() (guides.go:71-78), which lists each guide name and description. The board-link line is the boardInstruction constant (server.go:91), appended in hosted mode at server.go:100 when BoardURL is set. Side note, not a criterion: server.go:75 and server.go:76 are identical '- Locations:' bullets, so that line appears twice in the instructions text. Worth removing, but it does not affect this criterion.

internal/game/presence.go:732 starts a capTimer of t.WaitCap, and the wait loop's select (presence.go:863-872) returns WaitStillWaiting when it fires. The cap is 15s by default and at most 50s by validTiming (cmd/tcgreplay/main.go:130), so a call returns well under 60s. The cap timer is not reset between wakeups, so the call's total time is bounded. In internal/mcpserver/wait.go:112, KeepWaiting is true for still_waiting, and the default branch at wait.go:178 sets next to 'call wait_for_turn again now with since N, in this same reply'. internal/mcpserver/wait_test.go:252-254 (added in the diff) asserts KeepWaiting is true and next contains 'call wait_for_turn again'.

cmd/tcgreplay/main.go:117 sets maxWaitCap = 50s. validTiming (main.go:126-140) returns an error when WaitCap <= 0 or WaitCap > maxWaitCap. main() calls it at main.go:221-225 and exits with status 2 on error, so the playmat refuses to start. Any cap above 50s, including anything that could exceed 60s, is refused. cmd/tcgreplay/timing_test.go:42-63 (TestWaitCapInsideToolCallLimit) asserts that a 61s cap is refused, and that the default and the largest accepted cap are under 60s.

items.title: Tell ChatGPT who is signed in

goal.title: Tell ChatGPT who is signed in
criteria: Connected to the hosted playmat, asking who is signed in returns the player's identifier in the form OpenAI's profile rules require, and the same player gets the same identifier on a second connection.
Two different players get different identifiers, and the answer comes even when the playmat is full.
The desktop playmat's tools are unchanged.
The privacy page says the assistant is given the player's Google account ID to tell accounts apart.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: account.go:17-45 registers get_account with _meta openai/profile true, no input properties, and an output schema requiring a single string id with minLength 1 and pattern \S. The id comes from s.Account, which is Registry.AccountID (internal/usergames/mcp.go, diff hunk +1224-1232), reading acct.ID from hostauth.AccountFromToken (oauth.go:467-473, UserID). That ID is Google's sub (hostauth.go:75, google.go:191). hosted_account_test.go:52-104 (TestHostedGetAccount) checks the schema and the profile marker, and that a second connection for the same account returns the same ID as the first (lines 97-99). I could not check OpenAI's profile rules themselves, so the 'form they require' part rests on the schema the code declares and the test that checks it.

A different account gets a different ID: hosted_account_test.go:100-103 asserts userB's ID differs from DefaultAccount's. At the full cap, hosted_account_test.go:106-139 (TestHostedGetAccountAtFullCap) shows get_state refused as busy while get_account still returns userB.ID, and that asking takes no place. AccountID (usergames/mcp.go) touches no registry entry, and get_account is registered with mcp.AddTool outside the place-taking add/addWith path (account.go:23-24, 34-44).

Interpreting 'tools unchanged' as the set of tool names: the desktop list has exactly the 45 names in desktopToolNames (internal/mcpserver/annotations_test.go, diff hunk +502-515). TestDesktopToolNamesUnchanged (annotations_test.go, diff +517-539) compares against that list over both transports, and get_account is only added when Account is set (server.go, diff +67-69). Caveat: the descriptions, titles, jsonschema text and explicit-label encoding of the desktop tools all changed (server.go, guides.go, annotations.go). If 'unchanged' means identical definitions rather than names, this would not hold.

site/src/pages/privacy.astro, diff hunk @@ -193 (around lines 195-196): the 'Your AI assistant' item now says the playmat tells it your Google account ID (never your email address), so it can tell your accounts apart. site/e2e/privacy.spec.js (diff +137-141) asserts that text on [data-assistant-id].

goal.title: Answer OpenAI's domain verification
criteria: With the maintainer's token configured, `/.well-known/openai-apps-challenge` returns exactly that token as plain text, without signing in.
With no token configured, the address answers "not found", and nothing else on the playmat changes.
The token never appears in the playmat's logs or in the repository.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: cmd/tcgreplay/hosted.go:252 registers mux.Handle("GET "+openAIChallengePath, openAIChallengeHandler(challenge)) before the other routes; the handler (hosted.go:197-207) writes the trimmed token (main.go:207 TrimSpace of TCGREPLAY_OPENAI_CHALLENGE) with io.WriteString, Content-Type text/plain; charset=utf-8, Cache-Control no-store, and no newline. No auth wraps this route (a.Routes/RequireToken/RequireSession are not applied to it). hosted_routes_test.go TestOpenAIChallengeServed asserts 200, exact body, content type, no Set-Cookie. The env-driven path is covered by TestMainServesOpenAIChallengeFromEnv. The test was not re-run by me; the staged verification reports go test ./... passing.

hosted.go:199-201: when token is empty, openAIChallengeHandler calls http.NotFound, a plain 404 that is not the website's page. The only route added to hostedHandler is that one line (hosted.go:252); the rest of the mux is unchanged. TestOpenAIChallengeNotSet (hosted_routes_test.go) asserts 404, body differs from the site's 404, and no Location header. The other diff hunks (annotations, get_account, wait cap, privacy page) belong to other items in the same working tree and are not this criterion's concern.

Logging: the only log that mentions the token is the start-up line at hosted.go:479, which calls challengeText(c.openAIChallenge) (hosted.go:211-217). That prints only the fixed strings 'OpenAI domain token set' or 'no OpenAI domain token (...)'; the value is never printed. config.args() does not carry the value (grep finds no openAIChallenge reference in args), and the value is env-only, not a flag (main.go:73-75, 207). Repository: .do/app.yaml:9-17 declares the key as type SECRET with no value. A repo-wide grep for openai-apps-challenge and openAIChallenge found no literal token; the only literal is the fake testChallenge constant "oai-challenge-6f1d2c9a7b" in hosted_routes_test.go, which is a test stand-in, not the maintainer's token. items.title: Let the reviewer in past the player limit

goal.title: Let the reviewer in past the player limit
criteria: With the player limit reached by other accounts, the reviewer account still signs in, imports the example game and plays, while another non-reviewer account is still turned away.
An account with the reviewer's address that Google has not verified is treated like any other account.
The reviewer's place does not reduce the places available to other players.
With no reviewer configured, the limit works exactly as before, and the reviewer's address never appears in the logs or the repository.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: internal/usergames/usergames.go:118-136 (Use) lets the reviewer past a full cap (`(e == nil || !e.holds) && !reviewer && r.full()`), and Admit (line 142) and the board/MCP paths all go through Use. Sign-in reaches Admit at internal/hostauth/google.go:219. Non-reviewers still get hostauth.BusyError. cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_cap_test.go:218-260 (TestHostedReviewerPastCap) signs the reviewer in at cap 1, imports the site example battle-log.txt and mega-lucario deck, plays, passes the board sign-in, and checks a third account gets the busy page on connector and board.

usergames.go:164-166 isReviewer requires acct.EmailVerified, so an unverified account with the reviewer's address is not matched. The flag is carried from Google claims (internal/hostauth/google.go:141-191) through tokens (store.go:406-409, oauth.go:457-474), so tool calls get the same answer. Tests: internal/usergames/places_test.go TestUnverifiedReviewerEmailIsRefused, and cmd/tcgreplay/hosted_cap_test.go:239-248 where an unverified reviewer-address account is refused at the cap.

usergames.go:177-181 (full) counts only `e.holds && !e.reviewer`, so the reviewer's place never reduces the places available to others. The reviewer flag is set per Use (usergames.go:133). places_test.go TestReviewerPlaceNotCounted checks that with the reviewer in, A leaving lets C in and A can still take the one place while the reviewer holds one.

With no reviewer, cfg.Reviewer is "" and isReviewer returns false (usergames.go:164-166), so Use behaves as before. cmd/tcgreplay/main.go reads TCGREPLAY_REVIEWER only from the environment (trimmed, no flag). The start-up log only prints reviewerText ("reviewer account set" / "no reviewer account"), hosted.go:115-122 and 171. The telemetry recorder records the reviewer as a hashed id via r.ids.ID(email) (internal/telemetry/recorder.go:147-155), not the address. .do/app.yaml:25-27 declares TCGREPLAY_REVIEWER as a SECRET with no value. The only reviewer addresses in code are reviewer@example.com / Reviewer@Example.com in *_test.go files. Tests TestHostedReviewerUnsetKeepsTheCap and TestNoReviewerConfigured cover the unset case, and TestHostedReviewerPastCap asserts the address is absent from logs and events. Note for the caller, not a verdict: the staged diff also changes files outside this item's listed scope (Makefile, internal/mcpserver/*, site/src/pages/privacy.astro, site/e2e/privacy.spec.js, cmd/tcgreplay/timing_test.go), which look like other tasks' work, so the scope rule is likely broken even though these four criteria are met.

items.title: A listing icon without Pokémon trademarks

goal.title: A listing icon without Pokémon trademarks
criteria: The project holds a square listing icon, at least 512 pixels across and well under 5 MB, with its editable source beside it.
The icon shows no Poké Ball, Pokémon name, logo or character.
The website and board icons are unchanged.

scope.rule: Change only the files that belong to this item; change nothing that belongs to another task.

verdicts.evidence: plugin/assets/icon.png and plugin/assets/icon.svg are both untracked new files (tcgreplay.status lines 29-30). icon.svg:1 declares width="512" height="512" viewBox="0 0 512 512", so the source is square. Its comment at icon.svg:5-6 gives the render command (rsvg-convert -w 512 -h 512). internal/plugin/icon_test.go:22-54 (TestListingIcon, untracked) asserts the PNG decodes as png, is square, is at least 512 px, is at most 1 MiB (well under 5 MiB), and that the SVG source exists beside it. The verify line for go test ./internal/plugin passes, so that test passes. I could not read the PNG's pixel dimensions or byte size directly with my tools; that rests on the passing test.

I viewed plugin/assets/icon.png: it shows three fanned white-outlined plain cards, a cyan replay arrow with a play triangle on the front card, and a timeline strip with a dot. No Poké Ball, no text, no name, no logo and no character appear. icon.svg:1-37 contains only generic shapes, gradients and a title 'TCG Replay listing icon'. icon_test.go:48-53 also rejects the trademark words pokémon, pokemon, poké, poke ball, pokeball, pikachu and nintendo in the SVG source, and no match was reported.

tcgreplay.status (the staged status for tcgreplay) lists no changes to docs/logo.png, docs/icon.png or site/public/icon.png, and the diff (tcgreplay.diff) contains no hunk touching them. The verify command 'git status --short docs/icon.png docs/logo.png site/public/icon.png' passes with no output. The only icon paths changed are plugin/assets/icon.svg and plugin/assets/icon.png, which the goal allows.

goal.title: Build the plugin package
criteria: One command builds the plugin package, and building twice from the same sources gives the same contents.

The package shows the name "TCG Replay", connects to `https://tcgreplay.app/mcp` with the playmat's sign-in, and carries the icon, the description with the fan-project notice and credit, and the website, privacy, terms and support links.
The notice, credit, support link and address are taken from the project's existing sources, not typed into the listing.
